narrative:
Based on the assessment, your loan application was denied because the model determined there is a 43% chance you would struggle to repay the loan. While this means a 57% chance you would repay it successfully, the risk was still considered too high for approval.

The most significant factor pushing the decision toward denial was the length of your loan request. You asked to repay the loan over 48 months, while most approved applicants typically request around 19 months. A longer repayment period gives more time for financial circumstances to change and increases the bank's exposure to risk.

A second major factor was your credit history, which was rated as critical or containing other credits. This is a very strong signal of past difficulty managing obligations, and it pushed the decision further toward denial. However, this factor actually worked partially in your favor compared to other reasons—because your history isn't categorized as a past delay, it was less damaging than it could have been. Still, it remains a serious concern.

Finally, the status of your checking account contributed to the risk. With a balance between 0 and 200 DM, you had very little financial buffer at the time of application. Most approved applicants had no checking account at all, and only about 18% of approved applicants had a balance in your range, meaning this profile is associated with higher risk.

To improve your chances in the future, consider requesting a shorter loan term, building a stronger record of on-time payments, and increasing your savings buffer before reapplying.
